meta.title: A Week Before the Boat Trip

paragraphs: This is my diary for one week with the Explorers. My name is Lily. On Monday, I read a new email from my pen pal Grace in Singapore. Grace wrote, "On Fridays, my class plays cricket at school." I did not know this game. So I looked at the photo in her email. A boy in the photo held a long, flat, wooden bat. Then I wrote back and asked Grace how to play.

On Tuesday, Teacher Kim told the Explorers about our next trip. "On Saturday, we go sailing from the port," she said. "A sailing teacher will take us out on small boats." Every child got a note for a parent to sign. Mom signed my note at dinner. Dad asked, "Do you have a hat for the sun?" Pip sat under the table and waited for a piece of fish.

On Wednesday, I stayed at home after school. Tom had a part in the school musical. He practiced his song in the living room. He sang the same line five times. Pip put his head under a cushion. I laughed, and then I packed my bag for Saturday.

On Thursday, the Explorers met in the school library after lunch. Mia made a plastic cover for her camera. "The sea can make it wet," she said. Leo drew a poster with a blue boat and a big white sail. May checked the boat tickets and wrote the names of all the children. "Please do not be late on Saturday," said Teacher Kim. "The boat will not wait for us."

On Saturday, we went to the port at eight o'clock. The sailing teacher gave each of us a life jacket and a hat. First, he showed us a rope and told us how to hold it. Leo had trouble with the rope. It fell from his hands twice. Then the wind pushed the white sail, and our boat moved over the water. We sailed along the coast for a long time. Mia took photos from the boat. Her new cover kept the camera dry.

After an hour, the wind failed, and the boat stopped. "Is the boat broken?" asked Leo. "No, we only wait for the wind," said the sailing teacher. Nobody was afraid, and we watched the small waves. Ten minutes later, the wind came back. We sailed to the port, and everybody clapped. At home, I wrote this diary and told Pip about the boat. Tomorrow, I will write to Grace about our day.
